interactions.label: Emphasize
interactions.teaches: The learner sees the source figure as one continuous process while focusing attention on how four distinct input orbitals become four equivalent hybrids and then occupy tetrahedral directions

interactions.label: Show 109.5° angle
interactions.teaches: The tetrahedral bond angle is the equal separation between any pair of sp3 hybrid directions, but it is an annotation rather than part of the original orbital shapes
Rotating the scene reveals that the final four orange lobes are separated in three dimensions, not arranged as a flat four-petal drawing
Hovering identifies each orbital and reinforces that s, px, py, and pz are distinct before mixing, while the four sp3 products are equivalent after mixing

demo_steps.title: Complete flowchart
demo_steps.narration: All panels are visible at once, matching the textbook flow: atomic orbitals on the left, equivalent sp3 hybrids on the right, and the final tetrahedral arrangement below. The arrows show that these are stages of one hybridization process.

demo_steps.title: Start with distinct inputs
demo_steps.narration: The left block is emphasized: one spherical s orbital and three perpendicular p orbitals have different shapes and orientations. The large s and px labels remain clearly tied to their individual panels.

demo_steps.title: Hybridization makes four equivalent orbitals
demo_steps.narration: The right block is emphasized: the products are no longer labeled as s, px, py, and pz. Each orange sp3 hybrid has the same shape, with one large directional lobe and a small back-lobe.

demo_steps.title: Equivalent hybrids point tetrahedrally
demo_steps.narration: The bottom arrangement is emphasized: the same four sp3 hybrids now share one origin and point toward the corners of a tetrahedron. This geometry explains the tetrahedral directions used in molecules such as methane.

demo_steps.title: Optional bond-angle cue
demo_steps.narration: Turning on the angle label marks the ideal 109.5° separation between hybrid directions. It is optional so the figure can remain visually faithful to the original textbook diagram.

plan.geometry_notes: Use a fixed orthographic/axonometric textbook style with no panel replacement: the default must show the whole flowchart simultaneously. Overall world-space layout spans about 14 units wide by 9 units high. Place the atomic-orbital block in the upper-left, centered around x=-4.8, y=2.1; place the individual sp3 block in the upper-right, centered around x=3.6, y=2.1; place the final tetrahedral arrangement in the lower-right/bottom area, centered around x=3.9, y=-2.8. The rightward arrow runs horizontally from the atomic block toward the sp3 block at about y=1.8; the downward arrow descends from the sp3 block to the final arrangement at about x=3.7. Each small orbital panel occupies roughly 1.9 × 1.8 world units, with origins spaced about 2.1 units apart horizontally and 1.9 units vertically. Local triads in every panel span about 0.95 to 1.15 units from origin to arrow tip: +X screen-right, +Z screen-up, +Y receding diagonal up-right. Atomic block panel centers: s at approximately (-5.8, 2.8), px at (-3.7, 2.8), py at (-5.8, 0.9), pz at (-3.7, 0.9). The s sphere radius should be about 0.48 to 0.55, blue #6f9fe6, translucent/glossy. The p orbitals must be smooth, round, full teardrop or pear-shaped lobes, not thin cones: each p lobe length about 0.72 to 0.82 from the origin, maximum radius about 0.34 to 0.40, tapering smoothly to the nucleus. px is horizontal with red #e86b6b on -x and blue #6f9fe6 on +x. py lies along the displayed y diagonal with red on negative y/lower-left and blue on positive y/up-right. pz is vertical with blue upward and red downward. Labels 's', 'px', 'py', and 'pz' should be large, dark, italic serif text around 0.24 to 0.30 world-units high; place 's' directly below the sphere at about y=-0.75 relative to its panel origin, and 'px' directly below or slightly below-right of the horizontal p orbital at about y=-0.75 relative to its panel origin so it is not hidden by axes. Individual sp3 panel centers: top-left at (2.7, 2.9), top-right at (4.8, 2.9), bottom-left at (2.7, 1.0), bottom-right at (4.8, 1.0). Each sp3 orbital is orange/gold #f5a12a with highlights #ffd26a. Large lobe length should be about 0.95 to 1.10 from origin and maximum radius about 0.42 to 0.50, noticeably fuller and rounder than the axes; small back-lobe length about 0.25 to 0.32 and radius about 0.13 to 0.17. Individual hybrid directions in screen pose: one up, one right, one down-left/receding, one down. Final tetrahedral origin near (3.9, -2.8); final large lobes length about 1.15 to 1.30 and radius about 0.45 to 0.55, all equal in size, with small back-lobes about 0.25. Arrange final lobe axes as ideal tetrahedral vectors h1=(1,1,1), h2=(1,-1,-1), h3=(-1,1,-1), h4=(-1,-1,1), then rotate the tetrahedron to match the source pose: one lobe appears nearly vertical upward, one mostly right, one downward/front, and one down-left/back. Ideal angle between any two large-lobe axes is arccos(-1/3)=109.47 degrees. The optional angle label should be off by default and, when shown, should be small and unobtrusive near the final arrangement only. Arrows are medium gray #8c8c8c with filled triangular arrowheads; arrow labels are black or dark gray. Axes, axis labels, and central origin dots are black #000000. Guide rods are light gray #9a9a9a and thinner than axes. Emphasis interaction should not remove panels; it should brighten the selected section and dim nonselected sections to about 35% opacity while preserving the full layout and arrows.
plan.notes: Render orbitals as smooth implicit surfaces, metaballs, or high-resolution lathed/ellipsoid meshes with MeshStandardMaterial or Phong shading; avoid faceted or skinny lobes. Use at least 48 radial segments for lobes and sphere-like surfaces. Keep all labels as screen-facing text sprites or CSS2D labels so s and px remain readable and properly anchored during orbiting. The orbit control should rotate gently around the whole flowchart, but text labels should remain billboarded. For emphasisStep, do not switch panels on or off; change opacity, saturation, and perhaps add a subtle outline around the emphasized group. For showAngle=false, completely hide the 109.5° arc and text to preserve the textbook appearance.

authoredPrompt: This figure illustrates the sp3 hybridization process as a stepwise transformation, moving from four distinct atomic orbitals on the left to four equivalent hybrid orbitals on the right and finally to the tetrahedral arrangement they collectively produce at the bottom. The upper-left section shows the four pre-hybridization atomic orbitals drawn individually on Cartesian axes: a spherical s orbital (blue), a px orbital (two-lobed, red and blue, oriented along the x-axis), a py orbital (two-lobed, oriented along the y-axis), and a pz orbital (two-lobed, oriented along the z-axis). A rightward arrow labeled "Hybridization" leads to four equivalent sp3 hybrid orbitals, each rendered as a prominent orange lobe with a small back-lobe, shown individually pointing in different directions; a downward arrow then labeled "Gives a tetrahedral arrangement" leads to a final diagram in which all four sp3 orbitals appear simultaneously, with their large lobes directed symmetrically toward the four corners of a tetrahedron at 109.5° with respect to each other. This figure demonstrates how the mathematical mixing of one s and three p orbitals destroys the original orbital distinctions and produces four energetically and geometrically equivalent sp3 hybrids that underpin the tetrahedral bond angles observed in molecules such as CH4, NH3, and H2O.
authoredInteractions: - Toggle individual atomic orbital contributions (s, px, py, pz) on and off: isolate each orbital and see its role in forming the tetrahedral hybrid
authoredContext:
The valence orbitals of an atom surrounded by a tetrahedral arrangement of bonding pairs and lone pairs consist of a set of four sp 3 hybrid orbitals . The hybrids result from the mixing of one s orbital and all three p orbitals that produces four identical sp 3 hybrid orbitals ( ). Each of these hybrid orbitals points toward a different corner of a tetrahedron.

The hybridization of an s orbital (blue) and three p orbitals (red) produces four equivalent sp 3 hybridized orbitals (yellow) oriented at 109.5° with respect to each other.

A series of three diagrams connected by a right-facing arrow that is labeled, “Hybridization,” and a downward-facing arrow labeled, “Gives a tetrahedral arrangement,” are shown. The first diagram shows a blue spherical orbital and three red, peanut-shaped orbitals, each placed on an x, y, z axis system. The three red orbitals are located on the x , y and z axes, respectively. The second diagram shows the same four orbitals, but they are now purple and have one enlarged lobe and one smaller lobe. Each lies in a different axis in the drawing. The third diagram shows the same four orbitals, but their smaller lobes now overlap to form a tetrahedral structure.

A molecule of methane, CH 4 , consists of a carbon atom surrounded by four hydrogen atoms at the corners of a tetrahedron. The carbon atom in methane exhibits sp 3 hybridization. We illustrate the orbitals and electron distribution in an isolated carbon atom and in the bonded atom in CH 4 in . The four valence electrons of the carbon atom are distributed equally in the hybrid orbitals, and each carbon electron pairs with a hydrogen electron when the C–H bonds form.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The learner follows the figure’s progression from one s and three p inputs, to four equivalent sp3 hybrids, to their shared tetrahedral geometry

interactions.label: s contribution
interactions.teaches: The spherical s contribution is the equal, same-sign part present in every sp3 hybrid and gives each hybrid its large forward lobe

interactions.label: px contribution
interactions.teaches: The px contribution separates hybrids that point toward positive x from those with negative x character

interactions.label: py contribution
interactions.teaches: The py contribution supplies the front/back diagonal component needed to spread the four hybrids in three dimensions

interactions.label: pz contribution
interactions.teaches: The pz contribution gives upward versus downward character, completing the tetrahedral set rather than leaving the hybrids in a plane
Rotating the final arrangement reveals that the four orange lobes are separated in depth at tetrahedral angles, not merely drawn as a flat four-petal shape

demo_steps.title: Start with atomic orbitals
demo_steps.narration: The separate inputs are one spherical s orbital and three mutually perpendicular p orbitals. Their different shapes and orientations are visible before hybridization.

demo_steps.title: Mix into equivalent hybrids
demo_steps.narration: After hybridization, the original s, px, py, and pz orbitals are no longer shown as separate occupied shapes; their contributions combine into four equivalent orange sp3 hybrids.

demo_steps.title: Remove one contribution
demo_steps.narration: Turn off pz to see that the hybrids lose their full upward/downward separation. The tetrahedral geometry requires all three p directions plus the s component.

demo_steps.title: Restore the tetrahedron
demo_steps.narration: With s, px, py, and pz all included, the four equivalent sp3 orbitals point toward the corners of a tetrahedron with ideal bond angles of about 109.5 degrees.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an orthographic/axonometric textbook style, white background. Overall scene spans about 12 world units wide by 8 world units high. Default view should show only the selected stage rather than all source panels at once; preserve the source figure’s arrangement within each stage. Atomic-orbital stage: arrange four panels in a 2-by-2 block. Each local axis triad spans about 1.35 units from origin to arrow tip: +X screen-right, +Z screen-up, +Y diagonal up-right/receding. s sphere radius about 0.42 centered at origin, blue #7fa6e8 with translucent highlight. p orbitals use two teardrop/ellipsoid lobes length about 0.75 each side from origin and max radius about 0.32; px is horizontal with red #ee6a6a on -x and blue #6d9bd7 on +x, py lies along the y diagonal with red on -y/lower-left and blue on +y/upper-right, pz lies vertical with blue on +z and red on -z. Hybrid stage: four individual sp3 panels in a 2-by-2 block, each using orange/gold lobes #f6a02d to #ffd36b with a large forward lobe length about 0.95, max radius about 0.38, and a small opposite back-lobe length about 0.28, radius about 0.12. Individual hybrid orientations as seen in the source: one points up along +z, one points right along +x, one points down-left/back, and one points downward along -z. Final tetrahedral stage: one shared origin with four equivalent large lobes length about 1.05 from origin and small back-lobes about 0.22; orient one lobe nearly vertical upward, one mostly right, one downward, and one down-left/back to match the source drawing. Mathematically, the four ideal sp3 hybrids may be treated as h1=(s+px+py+pz)/2, h2=(s+px-py-pz)/2, h3=(s-px+py-pz)/2, h4=(s-px-py+pz)/2, then rotate the whole tetrahedron so the screen pose matches the figure. Ideal angle between any two large-lobe axes is arccos(-1/3)=109.47 degrees. When contribution toggles are off, omit that basis function from the displayed combination and renormalize visible hybrid amplitudes; if only one contribution is active, show the corresponding source-like component overlaid in the hybrid directions to make isolation clear. Process arrows are medium gray #8c8c8c; axes and labels are black #000000; gray guide rods are #9a9a9a.
interactionPlan.notes: Render orbitals as smooth implicit-lobe meshes or scaled metaball/ellipsoid surfaces with transparent Phong or MeshStandardMaterial gradients; use additive highlights to mimic the glossy textbook look. Keep axis labels as billboarded text sprites so they remain readable during orbiting. For the stage toggle, cross-fade between grouped panels rather than moving the camera abruptly. Contribution toggles should update both source-orbital opacity and the hybrid-combination mesh amplitudes, with disabled contributions ghosted or hidden consistently.

demo_steps.narration: The right block is emphasized: the products are no longer labeled as s, px, py, and pz. Each orange sp3 hybrid has the same shape, with one large directional lobe and a small back-lobe.

demo_steps.title: Equivalent hybrids point tetrahedrally
demo_steps.narration: The bottom arrangement is emphasized: the same four sp3 hybrids now share one origin and point toward the corners of a tetrahedron. This geometry explains the tetrahedral directions used in molecules such as methane.

demo_steps.title: Optional bond-angle cue
demo_steps.narration: Turning on the angle label marks the ideal 109.5° separation between hybrid directions. It is optional so the figure can remain visually faithful to the original textbook diagram.
